faqs.question: What is the Hyperion FT-IR Microscope used for?
faqs.answer: Hyperion is a research-grade FT-IR microscope used for chemical imaging and mapping, combining FT-IR and QCL laser imaging in one instrument, across pharma, forensics, semiconductor, and materials research.

faqs.question: What makes Hyperion the first of its kind?
faqs.answer: It's the first instrument to combine FT-IR and Infrared Laser Imaging (QCL) technology in a single device, supporting both in transmission, reflection, and ATR modes.

faqs.question: How much faster is QCL imaging than standard FT-IR imaging?
faqs.answer: QCL imaging at a single wavenumber runs at 6.4 mm² per second, against 0.1 mm² per second for full-spectrum FT-IR imaging, more than 60 times faster, at the cost of narrower spectral information per image.

faqs.question: How do I decide between FT-IR and QCL imaging for my sample?
faqs.answer: Collect a full FT-IR spectrum first to identify the wavelengths that matter for your sample, then switch to QCL imaging at those specific wavelengths to generate a fast chemical image in seconds.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the LN2-cooled and TE-cooled MCT detector?
faqs.answer: Choose the LN2-cooled MCT for maximum sensitivity where liquid nitrogen is available, or the thermoelectrically cooled MCT when you need high spatial resolution and sensitivity without a cryogen supply.

faqs.question: What is spatial coherence reduction, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: It's a patented technology that removes fringe and speckle artifacts from laser-based IR imaging, addressing a physical effect that occurs specifically in QCL microscopy and not in classical FT-IR, solved in hardware without slowing down the measurement.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Hyperion and the LUMOS II?
faqs.answer: Hyperion gives the user full manual control over every measurement parameter, while the LUMOS II automates the measurement process for a more guided workflow. Bruker positions them as different philosophies, not different capability tiers.

faqs.question: What FPA detector resolutions are available?
faqs.answer: 64×64 or 128×128 pixel, for diffraction-limited FT-IR imaging.

faqs.question: Can Hyperion data be correlated with Raman data from the same sample?
faqs.answer: Yes, using Co-Local Measurement, which transfers the same region of interest between Hyperion, LUMOS II, and SENTERRA II for combined IR and Raman analysis.

sections.title: FT-IR and QCL Imaging Modes
sections.tabSummary: When to use full-spectrum FT-IR versus fast QCL imaging
body: The choice between FT-IR and QCL imaging isn't about which is better. It's about what the measurement actually needs.

Full-spectrum FT-IR imaging via the FPA detector gives complete spectral information at every pixel, at 0.1 mm² per second. QCL imaging trades that breadth for speed: once you know which wavelengths matter, ILIM images at a single wavenumber at 6.4 mm² per second, more than 60 times faster. The patented coherence reduction is what makes that laser-based speed usable at all, removing the fringe and speckle artifacts that would otherwise compromise the image.

faqs.question: What is the LUMOS II FT-IR Microscope used for?
faqs.answer: LUMOS II is a stand-alone FT-IR and IR laser imaging microscope used for failure analysis, material research, and life science applications, across pharma, forensics, and environmental testing.

faqs.question: Does the LUMOS II need liquid nitrogen?
faqs.answer: No. TE-MCT is the standard detector, requiring no liquid nitrogen and no dry-air purge, though LN-cooled MCT is available as an option.

faqs.question: Is the LUMOS II suitable for beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes. The LUMOS II Wizard guides new users to correct results quickly, while experienced users retain full instrument control underneath.

faqs.question: How do I decide between single-point FT-IR, FPA, and ILIM imaging?
faqs.answer: Use single-point FT-IR for routine point measurements without cryogen requirements, FPA imaging for full-field chemical imaging at 1.6 mm² per second, and ILIM for the fastest possible imaging at a known wavelength, 4.5 mm² per second.

faqs.question: How do I image a round sample, like a filter, efficiently?
faqs.answer: Use FPA imaging with a circular measurement grid, which measures only the actual region of interest on round samples such as microplastic filters, saving significant time over a square grid.

faqs.question: Can I upgrade a single-point LUMOS II to FPA imaging later?
faqs.answer: Yes. The single-point FT-IR configuration is upgradeable to FPA imaging at any time, without replacing the instrument.

faqs.question: What is PermaSure+?
faqs.answer: PermaSure+ is Bruker's patented imaging calibration technology built into the LUMOS II for reliable, consistent imaging performance.

faqs.question: How large a sample can the LUMOS II accommodate?
faqs.answer: Up to 40 mm in height, with 270° access from three sides for straightforward sample placement.

faqs.question: Is the LUMOS II suitable for a regulated pharmaceutical environment?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's fully compliant with cGMP, GLP, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, and all major pharmacopeias, with automated OQ/PQ qualification testing.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the LUMOS II and the Hyperion?
faqs.answer: LUMOS II is faster at full-field FPA imaging and needs no cryogen, with guided, wizard-based operation. Hyperion is faster at single-wavelength ILIM imaging and gives the user complete manual control over every parameter.

body: LUMOS II doesn't force a choice at purchase. It offers three genuinely different ways to image a sample, and the right one depends on the question you're asking.

Single-point FT-IR, with TE-MCT as standard, is the starting configuration and needs no cryogen supply at all. FPA imaging adds full-field chemical imaging at 1.6 mm² per second with 1.25 µm spatial resolution in ATR, fast enough to make routine imaging genuinely practical. ILIM laser imaging trades some of that flexibility for raw speed at a single wavenumber, 4.5 mm² per second across a 1,800 to 950 cm⁻¹ range, in transmission and reflection.

longForm.heroHook: No liquid nitrogen needed. No steep learning curve either.
heroParagraphs: A research-grade FT-IR microscope usually asks something of you first: a cryogen supply, or a long training curve, sometimes both.

LUMOS II asks for neither. TE-MCT comes standard, so there's no liquid nitrogen and no dry-air purge to manage. The LUMOS II Wizard guides the measurement, so a new user gets a correct result fast, while an experienced one still has full control underneath.

Switch between single-point FT-IR, FPA imaging at 1.6 mm² per second, or IR laser imaging, all in the same instrument. Start with single-point measurement and add FPA imaging whenever you're ready, no replacement needed.

Its ATR crystal retracts on precision piezo motors, giving a clear view of the sample while the measurement happens exactly where you placed it. And with 270° access from three sides, getting the sample in position isn't a fight.
